name: 3 Colours Red
label: Creation Records
lede: Alan McGee called them the second best band in Britain, and in three years they had two Top 20 albums, a No. 11 single and a US tour with Aerosmith. Then they announced the split and played out the summer at Reading and Leeds.

eras.title: Four-track tapes in the post
eras.text: Two bassist-turned-songwriters from the British rock underground, one out of Diamond Head and one with a [[The Wildhearts|Wildhearts]] brother, built the band by mail. By the end of 1996 Alan McGee had them on Creation Records.

years.src: Wikipedia: 3 Colours Red · Wikipedia: Pete Vuckovic · Wikipedia: Chris McCormack
years.h: Pete Vuckovic and Chris McCormack meet through a friend, then write by post
years.p: [[Pete Vuckovic|88d7669e-4d48-4f11-a435-a1846a631ece]], ex-Diamond Head bassist, and [[Chris McCormack|536e5b92-ec29-4045-a8a2-4abc8dcaa604]], ex-Honeycrack, swap four-track recordings through the mail until they have songs.
years.xp: Vuckovic grew up in Tiverton, Devon, and played on Diamond Head's Death and Progress. McCormack, from South Shields, is the younger brother of Danny McCormack of the Wildhearts.

years.h: A pin in Time Out picks the name
years.p: Stuck at random into the listings magazine, the pin lands on an ad for Krzysztof Kieślowski's Three Colours film trilogy.

years.src: Wikipedia: Keith Baxter · Wikipedia: 3 Colours Red
years.h: Keith Baxter leaves Skyclad to play drums
years.p: [[Keith Baxter|ed0002f0-bbb6-437a-9abb-51dfdecb3bcb]] had made five albums with folk-metal band Skyclad. Manager Terry Thomas produces the demos.

years.h: Senseless Things founder Ben Harding joins on guitar
years.p: [[Ben Harding|b2165ff3-13bb-4b6f-a905-e3eb4786cacb]], a founder of Senseless Things, comes in for the demo sessions and stays.

years.h: First single on Fierce Panda, chart position 162
years.p: 'This Is My Hollywood' comes out on Fierce Panda. Creation reissues it later and takes it to No. 48.

years.h: Alan McGee signs them to Creation
years.p: McGee's ranking, per Wikipedia. The best, in his view, was his own [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]].

eras.title: Top 40, America, and out at Reading
eras.text: Two albums, six Top 40 singles and US tours with arena bands, all inside about three years. They announced the split in July 1999, with their biggest single six months behind them.

years.h: 'Nuclear Holiday' makes No. 22
years.p: The first Creation single. 'Sixty Mile Smile' follows and goes two places higher, to No. 20.
years.xp: 'Sixty Mile Smile' drew controversy over its references to Vuckovic being hospitalised after taking ecstasy, Wikipedia notes.

years.h: Pure, produced by the band's own manager
years.p: Fifteen songs recorded at Livingston Studios in London with Terry Thomas producing. It goes Top 20 with four Top 40 singles.
years.xp: The Sunday Times heard "a genetically engineered cross between the Clash and... the Ruts" and meant it kindly. The Guardian found the three-chord style deeply anachronistic.

years.cap: Pete Vuckovic, Chris McCormack, Keith Baxter and Ben Harding
years.h: On the road in America with Marilyn Manson and Aerosmith
years.p: At their peak the band tours the US with [[Marilyn Manson|5dfdca28-9ddc-4853-933c-8bc97d87beec]], [[Aerosmith|3d2b98e5-556f-4451-a3ff-c50ea18d57cb]] and Silverchair. At home, the Paralyse EP isn't eligible for the chart.

years.h: 'Beautiful Day', with strings, goes to No. 11
years.p: Their biggest hit, a power ballad produced by Dave Eringa. It reaches No. 40 on the US Radio and Records alternative chart in April.

years.h: Revolt puts pylons on the cover
years.p: A slicker second album, mostly produced by Eringa of [[Manic Street Preachers|32efea44-6cb5-4b4f-bdaa-c8b8f6cef981]] fame and mixed by Chris Sheldon. It peaks at No. 17.
years.xp: The pylon artwork was inspired by [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]]'s OK Computer. AllMusic felt it rattled on without leaving much of an impression; The Independent thought the band's ear for a tune got twiddled about in search of an arena sound.

years.src: Wikipedia: 3 Colours Red · Wikipedia: Revolt · Wikipedia: Pete Vuckovic
years.h: The split is announced; Reading and Leeds are the last shows
years.p: The band says it's over, citing musical and personal differences, and plays out the summer at the two festivals.
years.xp: Accounts differ on the cause. The band's Wikipedia page gives musical and personal differences; Vuckovic's own page ties the split to the unfair dismissal of their manager.

eras.title: Sony, America and Grand Theft Audio
eras.text: Nobody sat still. Vuckovic and Baxter got a major deal for a new band, McCormack went to America with an electro-rock outfit, and Harding left music for PR.

years.src: Wikipedia: 3 Colours Red · Wikipedia: Pete Vuckovic · Wikipedia: Keith Baxter
years.h: Vuckovic and Baxter sign to Sony as Elevation
years.p: They spend about two years on songs that never come out and are dropped. McCormack tours America with Grand Theft Audio, alongside the Wildhearts' Rich Battersby.

eras.title: Back, with a new guitarist
eras.text: Vuckovic and McCormack patched it up, Baxter came back, and an ex-Pornstar guitarist took Harding's place. The new album got good reviews on a small label, and the band stopped again in 2005.

years.src: Wikipedia: 3 Colours Red · Wikipedia: Keith Baxter
years.h: Vuckovic and McCormack make up, and the band is back
years.p: Baxter returns on drums after a short stint with [[Therapy?|85226286-349a-4046-8dcf-f75b32baa6b1]]. [[Paul Grant|b7093658-5c0c-4325-8027-b2c3d5fafe43]] of Pornstar replaces Harding.

years.h: The first Download Festival, and 'Repeat to Fade'
years.p: The band plays the first Download at Donington and returns to the singles chart at No. 97 with 'Repeat to Fade'.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Union of Souls · Wikipedia: 3 Colours Red
years.h: The Union of Souls, cut in an old BBC building in Swansea
years.p: On Mighty Atom, with Joe Gibb producing eight tracks and Chris Sheldon two. Jason Perry, Martin McCarrick and Alwyn Davies add vocals. Good reviews, few sales.

yt: "Beautiful Day" live at the Islington Academy
years.h: Japan, Die Toten Hosen, and a live record at Islington
years.p: Tours of Japan and of Europe with [[Die Toten Hosen|c3bc80a6-1f4a-4e17-8cf0-6b1efe8302f1]] and Donots. A show at the Islington Academy becomes the 2005 live album Nuclear Holiday and a DVD.

years.h: A farewell tour with the Yo-Yos, and a second split
years.p: Dropped by Sanctuary, disappointed by sales and still at odds, Vuckovic and McCormack call it again. Sanctuary's singles collection If You Ain't Got a Weapon... carries Vuckovic's sleeve notes.

eras.title: Camden, sculpture and a drummer gone
eras.text: After 2005 the members went into festivals and other people's bands. Vuckovic, based in London, now works as a sculptor, painter and writer, and put out a new song, 'I'm Gonna Die in New York City Tonight', in 2021.

years.src: Wikipedia: Keith Baxter · Wikipedia: 3 Colours Red
years.h: Keith Baxter dies at 36
years.p: The drummer had been playing with Lancaster band Baby Judas. His Wikipedia page gives the cause as liver failure.
years.xp: The band's Wikipedia page gives a gastrointestinal haemorrhage instead. Kerrang! and NME both ran tributes.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chris McCormack · Wikipedia: 3 Colours Red
years.h: McCormack starts Camden Rocks
years.p: A one-day festival across twenty Camden venues. He has also played guitar in [[Gary Numan|6cb79cb2-9087-44d4-828b-5c6fdff2c957]]'s live band and the reformed [[The Professionals|Professionals]].
